title: Aliexpress - experiences
body:
O.P.
HI guys,
i search i couldn't find a lot of discussion on it.
just wanted to see what was the general consensus on ordering through Aliexpress. i was going have have a go but note there isn't paypal so i held off! anything to watch out for?
i have used Bangood many times and never had issues. is it similar?
thanks

---- replies ----
[User #155807404 postsSnotty2000Hand me a fluffy white tissue!Whirlpool Forums Addict] inferno6688 writes...
but note there isn't paypal
That's all they offer me these days – although I may have clicked a checkbox in the recent past, as they never used to offer it.
Apart from long shipping times, I've never had an issue that hasn't been resolved to my satisfaction – if not for the long delays sometimes.
[User #275245900 postslambsI stand against genocide.Whirlpool Forums Addict] inferno6688 writes...
just wanted to see what was the general consensus on ordering through Aliexpress.
I've been using them for a number of years now without problems. Best way to avoid drop-shippers on ebay....and costs less. Sellers get a feedback score just like ebay, so check that out before choosing which to buy from.
Shipping is slow ATM due to COVID, but you have choices up to and including international couriers like UPS, which are expensive, of course. I generally choose AliExpress Standard shipping over the cheapest 'free' options. Costs a few $$ more but i am finding stuff arrives in 2-3 weeks as opposed to possibly months for 'free' shipping.
Ali collects GST on purchases as you're probably aware.
but note there isn't paypal so i held off!
I use a low credit limit CC and have never had a problem.
[User #858459127 postsDariusIIParticipant] Shipping and communications will be slower as Lunar New Year is in 2.5 weeks.
Goods sold are based in USD so the final amount may differ upon payment due to exchange rate and overseas transaction fee applies.
[User #275245900 postslambsI stand against genocide.Whirlpool Forums Addict] DariusII writes...
Goods sold are based in USD so the final amount may differ upon payment due to exchange rate and overseas transaction fee applies.
I have set my account on AliExpress to show everything in AUD (listing, cart, orders). Also the value of the orders I've placed matches exactly what appears in my CC account in AUD (ie what my CC has been charged). The CC I use has no international conversion or transaction fees.
[User #20426972500 postsTSQ\\//_Whirlpool Forums Addict] inferno6688 writes...
anything to watch out for?
Just read the description carefully and ignore the pictures. I've had a couple of things turn up that were not what I was expecting but were what I had actually ordered.
Otherwise no problems, I've bought lots of electronic components, small tools etc. The bonus is the surprise when a package finally arrives trying to remember what you've ordered.
[User #115203653 postspactrpoua.ten.looplrihw.wwwWhirlpool Forums Addict] i just had one where i ordered and they came back with it not being in stock and could i cancel it. They decided to up the price and relist the item. Seller had good feedback and their score was over 4 stars. I use a firefox extension called Aliexpress Enhancer so this seller was reported to them as a bad seller. I also looked for the same item and found the seller was selling it under another store name. Same page setup and everything.
[User #45470910386 postsexitguyWhirlpool Forums Addict] Interested in getting some stuff from AliExpress, been on their web site and a couple of ??
I want to use PayPal, but last time I went there it was not accepted – any change since last week. Bit confused as to which "store", some say "RU & EU Warehouses", some "China" – recommendations
[User #858459127 postsDariusIIParticipant] lambs writes...
Also the value of the orders I've placed matches exactly what appears in my CC account in AUD (ie what my CC has been charged).
Apologies. I was in the mind of "if i re-order the same item" or even go back to check how much I paid for each item in AUD, the AUD is slightly different due to conversion but the USD price, I believe, is unchanged. This is because the invoices and confirmation emails are in USD.
The CC I use has no international conversion or transaction fees.
Really depends on the CC and good to give the heads up to OP.
[User #465836821 postsMaccaGongWhirlpool Enthusiast] Use it all the time, bought expensive items as well. Issues are alway dealt with easy and in the buyers favour.
Pre Christmas I had aliexpress shipping down to under 3 weeks. Just bought stuff last week. See how it is now.
On a cool note. I bought 3 items from 3 different sellers and it seems with aliexpress shipping, they have combined all the items into one package.
[User #245473360 postswhirlpoolmuseWhirlpool Forums Addict] I use AliExpress quite regularly as well. It can be hard to tell the quality of items but i read the comments and reviews and base my purchase on that.
Last order I made was 31/12, arrived yesterday.
[User #6217141557 postsbigbudgieWhirlpool Enthusiast] The Mrs has over 2000 orders and spent over 50k on Aliexpress over the last4 years. Never had any fraud problems and it has only been since covid that 6 or so orders have gone astray
[User #1054343462 postsGuest1Whirlpool Forums Addict] exitguy writes...
I want to use PayPal
Last time I looked, PayPal is owned by eBay. Its not in their best interest to offer it on AliExpress. I think there was a time a lot of the Chinese sellers stopped on eBay due to the fees and went to AE. I don't shop much on eBay anymore, and mainly use AE.
[User #275245900 postslambsI stand against genocide.Whirlpool Forums Addict] Guest1 writes...
Last time I looked, PayPal is owned by eBay.
Not since around 2015. Completely separate businesses.
[User #715189153 postsHendorableParticipant] I signed up to aliexpress. Selected a product. Filled in all the details. When I tried to pay, an different amount was shown to that advertised ie the discount voucher amount had not been deducted (also they added VAT, assume it is GST, which I assume is kept out of the price to make it look better).
However I wanted the item (even if discount not applied) so filled in card details and entered to purchase. There was no indication that a transaction had occured. I checked my account information. My personal details ie name, address etc were properly recorded, but my card details were blank.
This was a concern so did some reseach on the company and it seemed ok so decided to have another go at purchase. This time I could not logon due to 'incorrect password'. I followed procedures provided to fix password. The process involved receiving an email and entering the code. This has to be done within 60 seconds. I did this a few times but could not get the email within 60 seconds so the process failed.
There is an option to contact customer service. I went through that process that simply referred me back to the process that did not work. Then I tried to logon again. A message advised the account did not exist. So I tried the forgot password process one more time and did not get an email, even after 60 seconds.
[User #552013016 postsDanster8I may be wrong but I doubt itWhirlpool Forums Addict] @Hendorable
You experience is fairly unusual. Aliexpress are not some dodgy purchase portal – they are one of the worlds largest shopping sites, possibly even larger than Amazon.
Yes, they don't include VAT/GST but will add it in when they realise the destination is Australia.
Regarding the incorrect password procedure, do you have a website to access your email in a faster way than possibly waiting for your normal email software (like Outlook or something else) to synch with your email provider?
You'll get an email after the purchase but I have had it take several minutes after the purchase before it appears in my inbox.
When you enter in your card deets for the purchase, there's a tickbox to tell Aliexpress to keep the card on file. I NEVER tick this as even though I trust (to a degree) their security, that degree is enough to not want them to have my card details on file.
Typically items take between 10 days upwards to get here. The fastest was about 10 days. The longest was something that arrived earlier this week from a purchase done on 20/11/2021.
